Expenses are calculated in terms of dollars per kilogram for different manufacturing locations by using total yielded labor intensity and energy use. These metrics are commonly measured by tonnes produced per year per full-time employee (t/yr per FTE) and kilowatt-hours of electricity and steam equivalent per kilogram of polysilicon produced (kWh /kg). Natural gas may also be included for FBR. Local ac labor rates (dollars per hour or equivalent annual salary per FTE) and utility rates (dollars per kilowatt-hour ac from the grid or produced locally) vary by manufacturing location. Figure 26 incorporates location-consistent 70 t/yr per FTE labor intensity and 55 kWh /kg electricity and ac steam equivalent and location-dependent labor and utility rates that are covered elsewhere (Woodhouse et al. Submitted). The principal input material for polysilicon production is mg-Si, which varies significantly in price across different periods and locations. Some information regarding mg-Si prices is publicly available (Shanghai Metals Market 2025), although the price paid for mg-Si can vary significantly from these spot price benchmarks and depends on volume. Moreover, polysilicon producers located outside China typically pay significantly more to import mg-Si from China (and pay shipping and tariffs) or pay more for the material from local suppliers. This is the most energy-intensive step in the c-Si supply chain, and utilities are a major cost driver for polysilicon production. Labor costs are also significant in the United States and Europe.
